passages:
Named machines may nest to arbitrary depth. There is one machine declaration
kind: the source `state` declaration is retired, not an alias or a second kind
of machine. Nesting restricts name visibility; it does not allocate data,
capture runtime bindings, retain an enclosing activation, or impose a stack
layout. Every nested declaration has its own signature, contract and identity.

A body consists of its executable portion followed by zero or more nested
machine declarations. The executable portion may finish with a transition,
result, or permitted Unit completion. A transition is not mandatory merely
because declarations follow. Once declarations begin, executable statements
cannot resume. This layout rule applies recursively. Nested declarations are
visible throughout their enclosing machine body, including before their textual
declaration, and within its nested declaration scopes. Duplicate declarations
follow ordinary name/overload rules; nesting is not a new overload mechanism.

Name resolution uses lexical scope. A helper is unavailable outside the machine
whose scope declares it; qualification cannot bypass this restriction. A sibling
can name another visible sibling, but cannot reach into that sibling's private
descendants. An ancestor's visible declaration may be called recursively; this
invokes its entry, not a saved activation or a private point inside its body.
Nested declarations are not separately package-exportable; package export of an
enclosing machine does not export its helpers.

Runtime parameters and locals of enclosing invocations are **not captured**.
Pass them explicitly, including references, capabilities and lifetime-bearing
values. Enclosing generic/static declaration bindings remain lexical context;
resolution and specialization retain their exact identities without creating an
implicit runtime environment. Nested contracts can use that static context and
their own parameters, not another invocation's local values or live facts.

An ordinary call resumes its continuation on normal return. A machine call in a
terminal `transition` arm forwards its normal result as the current invocation's
result, with no continuation in that invocation. A nested machine's return is
local to that invocation: it does not return from arbitrary lexical ancestors.
Both forms use the same contract, exact call acknowledgements and explicit
arguments. The distinction is call position, never nesting depth.
[Invocation contracts](state_contracts.md#terminal-calls-in-transition-arms)
owns argument, result, cleanup and fact obligations.

Resolution checks visibility and elaborates declaration context before erasing
lexical nesting into flat machine identities and explicit calls/transfers.
Source ancestry remains available for identity, diagnostics and debug mapping,
not as an executable parent stack. Downstream representations may have ordinary
basic blocks and jumps; these are not a revived source `state` construct.

passages:
A machine enters its own executable body; there is no separately authored entry
member. Trailing nested declarations scope helper names, not runtime data.
[Nested machines](machines.md#nested-machines-and-identity) defines visibility,
declaration order and flattening. Both ordinary and terminal calls invoke the
selected machine with ordinary explicit parameters. Context records and their
borrows are supplied like other arguments; no receiver or enclosing activation
is retained or rebound implicitly.
An ordinary terminal value, explicit return, or permitted implicit Unit
completion ends the invocation and owes its declared result/return contract.

A transition explicitly supplies the target machine's arguments. Executable uses
name the exact invocation's parameters or preceding local bindings; arrival
contracts use the target's parameters. Enclosing and sibling runtime bindings cannot be
recovered by matching spelling. Nominal member and case selection retains the
declared owner, including payload projections rooted at an explicit context argument.

Machine `requires` applies at every invocation, including terminal and recursive
calls. Every arrival establishes the target's requirements and declared domains
under actual argument substitution. Nesting does not assume the parent's entry
requirements again, import its return guarantees, or supply facts invalidated
by mutation. Live caller facts can discharge a nested helper's requirements;
body inference must justify any inferred private requirements on every arrival,
not grant them from lexical ancestry. Every invocation retains both sides of
its own contract. A recursive contract is not its own proof; induction follows
the well-founded obligations in [termination](termination.md).

Arrival substitution is simultaneous and identity-based. Scalar arguments retain
their evaluation snapshots; facts about referenced storage must survive writes
from later arguments. A same-named formal cannot alias an unrelated caller value.
Every reachable predecessor participates in a join. Unknown input cannot be
omitted to preserve a convenient invariant. A minimum collection length is not
an exact extent, and declaration initializers are not recurring loop invariants.
## Terminal calls in transition arms

Resolve every called target as a machine, nested or otherwise. A terminal call
is an invocation whose normal result completes the current machine, including Unit completion.
Argument admission, result compatibility, machine postconditions, cleanup,
crash and no-normal-return behavior are the ordinary call-and-completion rules.
Only the selected arm executes, with ordinary once-only operand evaluation.

Terminal machine calls accept the same exact operational acknowledgements as
other calls:

This invokes `Storage::read` in the current activation and forwards its normal
result; it does not start or detach a task. If the call parks, completion of the
enclosing machine remains pending. No return, cleanup or storage reclamation
occurs merely because the call is syntactically final or becomes suspended.
Ordinary cleanup-bearing completion edges still discharge their obligations.
Tail-call lowering may remove unnecessary control state only while preserving
all live backing, loans, custody and completion obligations. Recursive runtime
calls still obey the no-accumulated-frames rule.

Nested machine calls have no marker exemption. Their exact call envelope
determines `suspend` and `block`, including in terminal position, even when
lowering later implements the call with a jump. Markers do not redirect name
resolution. Missing, partial or redundant call markers reject under
[effects](effects.md#call-site-acknowledgements). The same
[borrow/carry requirements](../resources/carry.md#borrows-across-suspension)
apply in a terminal arm as at any other suspending call.
